title: BOX OF PORTUGUESE PITCHER, ISR...
reason: Title hides a hand-modelled flower-encrusted lidded porcelain vase in Coalport/Rockingham style (unmarked in photos, base not shown) plus a cobalt and gilt Victorian-style bowl; worth a base check.
findings: Ten loose items; the title mentions only the Portuguese pitcher and Israeli glass bowl. Best piece is a flower-encrusted lidded vase (pot pourri or sugar form) with hand-modelled applied roses, poppies, forget-me-nots and a tulip finial, a pierced cover, gilt scalloped rim and scroll feet, in the style of Coalport or Rockingham 'Coalbrookdale' encrusted porcelain of about 1830-50 (could be a later copy); no mark is visible and the base was not photographed, so maker and age are unverified. Also a cobalt blue and gilt English-style porcelain footed sugar bowl with floral panels and scroll handles (lid missing); a Portuguese-style jug with a stylised blue and red bird and flowers (no mark visible); a frosted grey-lilac Israeli glass bowl with drip decoration (no signature seen); an amethyst glass ball; a modern red carved-resin lacquer apple box and a red resin sleeping boy figure; a small cast metal imp figure with a peg (looks like a bottle opener or fitting); and a brass cockerel. No marks or signatures readable in any photo.
condition: The encrusted vase looks intact with no obvious flower losses in the photos, though small petal chips are hard to rule out; the cobalt bowl has rim staining, gilt wear and no lid; the other items look sound.
rescore_note: Unmarked, apparently intact flower-encrusted pot pourri vase and cover in English Coalbrookdale style (c.1830-60 if genuine, but base unseen so maker and age unproven and a later copy is quite possible), plus modest extras (lidless cobalt and gilt bowl, Portuguese jug, Israeli glass bowl); mix lands at the top of the $80-200 band. No comp seen.
